question.problem: Given the **orthonormal** basis $B=\{[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -1\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]\}$ of ${R}^{2},$ find $[x]_{B}$ if $x=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -5\end{aligned}].$
question.worked_solution:
Let's denote the vectors of $B$ as ${q}_{1},\,{q}_{2}.$ 

Since $B$ is an orthonormal basis, we have that $[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]$, where ${x}_{i}=x\cdot {q}_{i}.$ Computing the components of $x,$ we get the following: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -5\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}0 \\ -1\end{aligned}]=0+5=5 \\ {x}_{2} & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -5\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=-2+0=-2\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have 

$$
[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}5 \\ -2\end{aligned}].
$$
